transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Daniel Cho - Redwood; Lara Kim, Tom Reyes, Priya Nair - Sentinel Insights

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. this is maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. daniel is our SE, he'll run the optimize walkthrough focused on quant profiles — int8 and fp8, quality vs latency.
[00:07] Lara: yep hi thanks, we want to understand the tradeoffs — our prod latency p95 is around 220ms today and cost is getting out of hand.
[00:12] Daniel: cool, quick agenda — show profile results, talk through quality metrics we use (perplexity / rouge-ish for retrain-ish tasks), latency numbers, then next steps for a benchmark on your workload.
[00:20] Tom: quick context, we're currently on a mix of hosted endpoints and a small k8s infra, models are a custom 13B derivative, using kv cache in our serving layer.
[00:27] Daniel: got it. couple quick questions — sequence length distribution, avg  tokens per request?
[00:30] Tom: average 120 tokens, tail to 600 for long summaries.
[00:35] Daniel: perfect — that matters for quantization impact and kernel selection.
[00:40] Maya: also to note sentinel has SOC2 in flight and key mgmt needs, which we'll cover in separate security doc.

[05:15] Daniel: okay jumping into the slides — here's an example profile we ran on a 13B LLM: baseline fp16 -> int8 -> fp8 (hybrid) numbers. quality drop for int8 depends a lot on task, but for short completion tasks we often see <1% relative quality drop; for retrieval-augmented generation with many instruction tokens there's slightly higher delta.
[05:40] Lara: when you say quality drop, what metric exactly? we've got a human eval set for our summarization.
[05:45] Daniel: ideal is to use your human eval set. we typically show automated proxies: bleu/rouge/bertscore depending on task, plus perceptual human testing. in our internal tests on summarization 13B, int8 had ~0.8 BLEU drop and fp8 ~0.2, but latency improved a lot — p95 down from ~220ms to ~140ms on the same GPU for int8 in many cases.
[06:10] Priya: wait fp8 improved latency too? i thought fp8 is primarily a quality-preserving object with some perf gains.
[06:15] Daniel: yes fp8 sits between fp16 and int8: fp8 often keeps quality close to fp16 while giving kernel-level speedups (depending on h/w support). int8 gives the largest throughput wins but can need per-layer calibration and sometimes a small quality regression.

[09:00] Tom: we're worried about hallucinations increasing after quant. we've seen weird artifacts before after quantize. how do you guard?
[09:10] Daniel: great question. three levers — 1) selective quantization: keep critical layers in fp16, quant rest; 2) post-quant eval with your eval set and focused prompts; 3) run regression detection integrated into Redwood Optimize — we flag quality regressions and can auto-fallback to a higher-precision variant on rollout.
[09:32] Lara: selective quantization sounds promising. can we control per-layer?
[09:35] Daniel: yes we expose quant profiles: full-int8, mixed-int8, fp8-hybrid. you can pin profiles per model or route.

[12:00] Daniel: demo time — i'll pull up a live run we did for a customer similar to you: dataset of 1k samples, compared fp16 vs int8 vs fp8. showing latency histogram and token-level mismatch rate.
[12:18] (screen share noise)
[12:30] Daniel: ok, here: p50/p95/p99 charts — int8 p95 roughly 40% lower than fp16 in this run. fp8 sits around 15-25% lower. cost per token drops accordingly.
[12:50] Lara: numbers look good. how about batching? we do batch at the inference layer and sometime see increases in queueing latency.
[12:58] Daniel: batching is another win for throughput but yes it can widen tail. Redwood Optimize suggests batching targets and dynamic batch windows based on SLOs — you can trade a little p50 to shrink p95. plus prefix/KV cache reduces repeated compute for conversational flows.

[16:20] Tom: our tail tokens are long — caching helps?
[16:25] Daniel: yes, KV cache is huge for multi-turn. also prefix caching for common prompts. in some customers caching reduced token compute by 30-60% depending on repetition.

[19:00] Priya: curious about hardware — do these fp8/int8 gains assume A100 or M200? our infra has mix of A10 and A100.
[19:10] Daniel: hardware matters. some fp8 kernels are optimized for latest hw (H100-level) and A100 has good int8 support; A10 is more constrained. Redwood's runtime picks kernels per hw and we've got presets. we'll surface recommended profiles per GPU in the Optimize console.

[22:00] Lara: what's the rollback story if quality drops post-rollout?
[22:05] Maya: we support canary rollouts and automatic rollback triggers tied to your evaluation prompts. if we see regression above threshold we can auto-fallback to previous profile.

[25:00] Daniel: quick note on model fallbacks: you can route to cheaper model variant for non-critical paths and keep high-quality model for payment-critical flows.

[28:30] Tom: pricing questions — is Dedicated necessary to get these kernel-level gains?
[28:40] Maya: not necessarily. Hosted can run optimized kernels and quant profiles; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and sometimes better latency stability and compliance controls. for strict SLOs Dedicated + private network might be recommended.

[32:00] Lara: ok so next step we'd like Redwood to run a bench on our 1k sample set to see real quality vs latency numbers. also need the security docs for SOC2 and KMS.
[32:10] Maya: we'll do that. daniel will share the scripts and run the bench. we'll aim for results by 2026-05-11.

[34:00] (short cross talk)
[34:12] Daniel: one more tip — sometimes int8 can be tuned with small calibration datasets to reduce regressions a lot. that's low effort and we include it in the pilot.

[38:00] Priya: timeline — if bench looks good, pilot for 4 weeks and then move to Dedicated? approx costs?
[38:12] Maya: yes typical pilot is 2-4 weeks. i'll attach pricing bands — hosted pilot vs dedicated commit estimates.

[41:30] Lara: any known incompatibilities with our on-prem KMS?
[41:40] Daniel: no major ones; we integrate via standard KMS APIs and can support customer-managed keys for Private. we'll get your security team the integration notes.

[43:50] Maya: recap: 1) Redwood to run benchmark on 1k samples (Daniel), 2) share quant guide + scripts (Daniel), 3) send pricing and pilot options (Maya), 4) schedule follow-up the week of 2026-05-18.
[44:05] Tom: sounds good. thanks all.
[44:10] Maya: thanks, talk soon.
